title.narrative: Integrated assistance for Urban Afghan Refugees and Host Communities in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) and Balochistan Provinces

description.narrative: 1. Afghan refugees (urban settings) - men and women 2. Youth Afghan and host – 18-30 years of age

Relief International implemented a six-month pilot project titled 'Integrated Assistance for Urban Afghan Refugees and Host Communities in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan Provinces' to address the immediate and long-term needs of Afghan refugees and host communities residing in six districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) and Balochistan. RI implemented the proposed activities with urban refugees living in Peshawar and Nowshera districts in KP. Additionally, Relief International conducted a comprehensive study in Balochistan to investigate and analyze the dynamics of social cohesion between Afghan refugees and Pakistani host communities. The research sought to identify key factors influencing mutual understanding, cooperation, and integration.

key objective of the project: Afghan refugees have improved resilience, self-reliance, economic empowerment, and increased chances of living a healthy, safe, and dignified life Results/outcomes:Result-1: Afghan and host communities have strengthened their capacities and attained improved access to essential services in Peshawar and Nowshera districts of KP provinceResult-2: Youth Afghan and host communities (aged 18-30 years) have expanded access to home-based skills development and sustainable income generation activities in Peshawar and Nowshera districts of KP province;Result-3 Knowledge enhanced and learning disseminated to support the recovery of Afghan refugees’ livelihoods, education, protection, and factors influencing social cohesion in Quetta, Pishin, Chaman and Chaghi districts of Balochistan province
